name: OH-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+12 district with a long-serving Republican incumbent seeking re-election
Fundraising gap of more than 100-to-1 favors Latta ($1.46M vs $11.7K)
Prediction markets price Latta's win chance around 94%
No public polling or outside spending signals any Democratic viability
model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Latta's incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of more than 100-to-1 leave the Democratic challenger with no visible path. Prediction markets price the incumbent near 94%, and the absence of any polling attention or outside investment in the race points to an easy win.
model.watch: Only a major late-breaking scandal or an unusually large Democratic wave would put the outcome in doubt, and even then the seat would likely remain Republican.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Ohio's fifth district leans firmly Republican, and longtime incumbent Bob Latta is seeking another term after securing renomination. His Democratic challenger, Brian Shaver, has run a minimal campaign, raising roughly twelve thousand dollars against Latta's nearly one and a half million, and no outside groups have invested on either side. No public polls have surveyed the general election, and prediction markets give Latta about a ninety-four percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district's partisan lean, a favorable environment for Republicans, incumbency advantages, and the overwhelming financial gap all favor Latta. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot and may draw a small share of votes. The forecast expects Latta to win comfortably, with the only real question being the size of his margin rather than the outcome itself.
